title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Model with Heterogeneous Evidence Integration for Clinical Prognosis
abstract: arXiv:2610.13510v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clinical prognosis requires integrating structured measurements, physiological waveforms, longitudinal history, and population context. We introduce PRISM (Population-Retrieved Inference for Structured Multimodal Prognosis), a multimodal language model that combines per-feature numerical tokenization, recency-weighted aggregation of longitudinal ECGs, and a dual-modality population memory bank. Retrieval operates in representation space: the model receives mean-pooled embeddings of similar training-cohort encounters, while no individual retrieved record enters the prompt. On the 1,443-task MDS-ED benchmark, PRISM achieves AUROCs of 86.2% for diagnosis, 93.1% for deterioration, 91.8% for ICU admission, and 92.8% for mortality. These results use a 96-hour pre-arrival window unavailable to reported baselines. With benchmark-window inputs only, PRISM reaches 0.8895 AUROC, compared with 0.8937 for UniPACT and 0.8889 for MDS-ED. A matched-inpu

translated_title: 面向临床预后预测的检索增强异构证据融合多模态语言模型
translated_abstract: 临床预后预测需要整合结构化测量指标、生理波形、纵向病史以及人群背景信息。我们提出了PRISM（基于人群检索的结构化多模态预后推断），这是一种多模态语言模型，它结合了逐特征数值标记化、纵向心电图的近期加权聚合以及双模态人群记忆库。检索在表示空间中进行：模型接收相似训练队列就诊记录的均值池化嵌入，而任何单独的检索记录都不会进入提示词中。在包含1,443个任务的MDS-ED基准测试上，PRISM在诊断任务中达到86.2%的AUROC，在病情恶化预测中达到93.1%，在ICU入院预测中达到91.8%，在死亡率预测中达到92.8%。这些结果使用了96小时的到院前时间窗，而所报告的基线方法无法获得该时间窗的数据。仅使用基准时间窗内的输入时，PRISM达到0.8895的AUROC，相比之下UniPACT为0.8937，MDS-ED为0.8889。
tldr: 该论文提出了PRISM，一种通过双模态人群记忆库在表示空间中检索相似病例嵌入、并融合异构临床证据的检索增强多模态语言模型，在包含1,443个任务的MDS-ED临床预后基准上，于诊断、病情恶化、ICU入院和死亡率预测等多项任务中取得了优异表现。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces PRISM, a retrieval-augmented multimodal language model that integrates heterogeneous clinical evidence via representation-space retrieval of similar cohort encounters from a dual-modality population memory bank, achieving strong performance on the 1,443-task MDS-ED benchmark across diagnosis, deterioration, ICU admission, and mortality prediction.
